items.title: Live: 'Another world is possible': Calls for unity at Winter Olympics opening
items.description: The 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Olympics are here, launched in an historic opening ceremony held in a number of Italian locations simultaneously. Follow all the action in our live blog.

items.title: A bigger economic story is unfolding beyond interest rates
items.description: As the opposition and government wrestled in the hay barn over who's to blame for this week's Reserve Bank interest rate increase, there's a much bigger story unfolding in the wings.

items.title: How Epstein's ties to the 'Prince of Darkness' could bring down Britain's PM
items.description: Sir Keir Starmer led Labour to a landslide election victory two years ago, but in the past week, things have unravelled for the British prime minister. What went wrong?

items.title: Herzog's Australia visit unfortunately links two previously separate events
items.description: Unravelling the threads of antisemitism and anti-Israeli sentiment will require both more political courage and more community tolerance than we have seen to date.

items.title: PFAS plume linked to historic tanker crash and decommissioned dump
items.description: For 25 years this waterway was polluted with toxic "forever chemicals". It was only disconnected from a major drinking supply 18 months ago.

items.title: Almost every Australian corner to pick up rain this week
items.description: Almost every corner of Australia will pick up rain during the next seven days, including heavy falls and pockets of flooding in multiple states.

items.title: Nancy Guthrie may have been abducted in a 41-minute window
items.description: Nancy Guthrie was last seen alive when a relative dropped her outside her Tuscan home after a family games night. The 84-year-old grandmother has now been missing for a week.

items.title: Adelaide Writers' Week saga 'probably was preventable', festival director says
items.description: As Adelaide Writers' Week went up in flames, Julian Hobba contemplated resigning as Adelaide Festival's executive director. He now says "we needed to trust the judgement" of the literary event's former leader, Louise Adler.

items.title: Stuck without a team? Here's who to support at the T20 cricket World Cup
items.description: As another T20 World Cup sneaks up on us, here's everything you need to know about the tournament, including a guide on how to pick which team to support, depending on your needs.

items.title: Even a criminal conviction can't taint 'good bloke' status
items.description: The rich and powerful were all too happy to maintain connected to Jeffrey Epstein until it became the less convenient option.

items.title: Inside the 'textbook' search for Gus Lamont
items.description: A retired police officer who helped pioneer search guidelines used during the investigation into the disappearance of Gus Lamont, praises the efforts to find the missing boy and expresses support for the detectives' conclusions.

items.title: 'Do not try this at home': Controversial contact sport sells more than 5,000 seats
items.description: The Run Nation Championship will see two athletes run at each other, in a sport criticised for its head injury risks. Organisers argue the championship has been professionalised, and will grow to be as big as boxing.

items.title: Breaking: Three men dead after light plane crash, SA police say
items.description: Police were called to the Long Bay area near Goolwa South on Friday afternoon after reports of a light plane crashing into the ocean.

items.title: How a cheating socialite orchestrated her high-flying husband's murder
items.description: The brutal killing of a high-flying hotelier in his Brisbane mansion led to decades of rumour, myth and speculation about what unfolded on that fateful night.

items.title: Trump posts, then deletes, video depicting Obamas as monkeys
items.description: The video also included several debunked conspiracy theories linked to the 2020 US election, which the president has falsely claimed was stolen from him.

items.title: Justice, healing, truth: Elders call for change after alleged terror attack
items.description: For Noongar elders, the alleged attack on Borloo/Perth is viewed against the background of a long history of violence. They are calling for a truth-telling commission to heal deep scars and help to combat racism.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Test your knowledge of Gladiator, James Bond and your right to party
items.description: Every question has only two options: One is right and the other is wrong. You have an even chance of guessing correctly each time.

items.title: Ouyen may have recorded a heat record, but we will probably never know
items.description: It was tipped to be one of the hottest places on Earth last week, but we may never know exactly how hot it got in Ouyen — at least officially.

items.title: Why home loan repayments aren't included in official inflation figures
items.description: Mortgage repayments are going up, but they aren't included in the key official inflation figure, the consumer price index. Here's why.

items.title: India's 14yo batting prodigy breaks records in World Cup final
items.description: The 14-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi breaks Alyssa Healy's record with the highest score ever in a World Cup final to power India to the global under-19 crown.

items.title: Martin Luther King III says dad's 'dream' possible for First Nations people
items.description: Martin Luther King Jr's son says while the US administration was "attempting to turn the clock back" on equal rights, Australia shows "potential".

items.title: RBA governor grilled over rising inflation as political fight heats up
items.description: RBA governor Michele Bullock has refused to blame the Albanese government for rising inflation, as a political fight breaks out in the wake of the bank's rate hike.

items.title: I have a question for the men who had no questions about Epstein
items.description: The millions of pages of documents related to the late convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein have shone a light on how many influential men were ready to disregard the experiences of countless women.

items.title: Why it took police nine days to declare the Invasion Day attempted bomb attack in Perth terrorism
items.description: When a homemade fragment bomb was allegedly thrown into a crowd on January 26, it took nine days for it to be declared an act of terrorism. The WA police commissioner explains why, as Indigenous leaders raise concerns.

items.title: Iran says 'wall of mistrust' with US should be overcome after talks in Oman
items.description: The two countries held talks mediated by Oman in Muscat after weeks of tensions between Washington and Tehran.
